text: A Stream only watches. This lesson writes the piece that actually acts: two Tasks, both reading from the same Stream, each with a genuinely different job against the two shared tables from Lesson 2.

The first Task keeps ticket_facts current for Support. It's a true upsert: WHEN MATCHED updates a ticket's status, priority, and category; WHEN NOT MATCHED inserts a brand new ticket. If this exact MERGE happened to run twice against the same change rows, the UPDATE branch would just set each column to the same value a second time. That property has a name: idempotent. Hold onto that word.

The second Task appends refund events for Finance, and it looks different on purpose: no WHEN MATCHED branch at all, only WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT, because refund_events is append-only by design — each row is a distinct refund event, not a value to overwrite. But that design choice has a real cost: this MERGE is not idempotent. Feed it the same stream rows twice, and it can insert the same refund event twice.

Both Tasks query the very same Stream, tickets_stream, as two independent consumers. Snowflake does support this. What it doesn't protect you from is two Tasks both reading the same not-yet-advanced data in overlapping windows — and that gap behaves very differently depending on which of these two Tasks you're talking about.

One more thing before moving on: a newly created Task doesn't run on its schedule yet. It's created suspended, as a deliberate safety default. Next lesson actually resumes both Tasks and watches them run for real.
